subject: Latency gatekeeper evaluation — hosted API vs incumbent (p95/p99 + streaming)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
To: Samir Kaur <samir.kaur@noriahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Mar 2028 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed latency qualification plan

Hi Samir — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and a concrete path for the latency/SLO qualification you asked about (p95/p99 end-to-end for user-facing requests, and streaming behavior for conversational flows).

Summary of Noria requirements (from call):
- Peak steady-state: ~600 qps (spiky bursts to ~1k qps for 30s)
- Typical request size: 120–250 tokens request / 60–160 tokens response
- Strict p95 target: <= 120 ms E2E (cold-cache excluded)
- p99 target: <= 420 ms E2E
- Streaming: support chunked SSE token-by-token with first-token latency < 50 ms and per-chunk tail < 80 ms
- Concurrency: up to 300 active concurrent streaming sessions

What Redwood will validate in the benchmark:
1) End-to-end p95/p99 on your traffic envelope (hosted API run vs incumbent provider snapshot you provided)
2) Concurrency and streaming tail behavior under realistic session churn (connect/disconnect)
3) Throughput sustainability with KV/prefix caching warmed (and cold-warm delta)
4) Fallback behavior: hosted -> quantized model variant if capacity constrained

Suggested test windows and deliverables:
- Synthetic baseline run (controlled): 2h window, 600 qps steady with 1k qps 30s spikes; we’ll produce p50/p95/p99, throughput, token/sec, and drop/timeout rates.
- Streaming stress run: 90 minutes with 300 concurrent sessions (mix of 30s/2min sessions) to capture first-token and chunk tail distribution.
- Incumbent comparison: we’ll replay your sample traces (you mentioned you can share NDJSON traces) and compare E2E metrics side-by-side.

Action items I propose now:
- Samir: share the anonymized trace bundle and confirm preferred 2h benchmark window (we can run as early as next Tue 03/06). Attachments: we’ll accept NDJSON or gzipped logs.
- Laura: I’m looping you to sign off on the test harness and define host/instance sizing for the hosted run.
- Ben: please prepare a draft traffic model (token distribution + session length) for the synthetic run so we can map to cost estimate.

Attachments: blank SLO matrix template (noria_slo_matrix_v1.xlsx) attached — please fill fields marked in yellow if you want any bespoke constraints included.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a proposed calendar invite once Samir confirms the trace upload.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com]
From: Samir Kaur <samir.kaur@noriahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed latency qualification plan

Thanks Jordan — this is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications before we lock the window: 

1) Incumbent baseline: our current provider reports p95 ~185 ms, p99 ~560 ms on production (these are what we see at the edge after our auth/waf layers). We want to be confident hosted can get to <=120/<=420 on our envelope (post edge).

2) Traces: attached is a sanitized bundle (sample_traces_20280301.ndjson.gz). It contains per-request timing (edge ingress, model request/response timestamps) and token counts. We removed PII.

3) Traffic nuances: about 35% of calls are short prompts (<80 tokens total) and 20% are long multi-turn conversations where streaming matters. Also note we have a burst pattern around 11:00 PDT daily.

4) Test window: Tue 03/06 at 09:00 PDT works for us for the 2h run. If Redwood needs more lead time for instance sizing say so.

I’ll also share a short doc with our SLAs/penalty matrix privately after the warmup run.

– Samir
Samir Kaur
Head of Platform Engineering, Noria Health
[platform@noriahealth.com]
Attachment: sample_traces_20280301.ndjson.gz (sanitized)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed latency qualification plan

Looping in quick technical notes for the test harness and suggested acceptance criteria.

Notes:
- Baseline sizing: for an apples-to-apples hosted run we’ll provision 8xA100 equivalent workers (we’ll document exact SKU and kernel choices) with autoscale headroom for the 1k qps spike.
- Warm cache vs cold: we’ll run a warm-warmed baseline (KV cache + prefix caching enabled) and then a cold reset pass to show delta. Please expect cold p95 to be materially higher; our acceptance gating is on warmed runs unless you require cold-start SLAs.
- Measurement: we’ll measure E2E at the same ingress point you provided (i.e., after your auth/WAF timestamps) so numbers are comparable to incumbent. We’ll also export raw request traces in NDJSON so you can run your own parsing.
- Streaming: for first-token latency we’ll target <= 45 ms on warm runs; chunk tail target <= 75 ms. Our streaming harness will use jittered token emission to replicate multi-turn user typing.

Suggested acceptance gates (proposal):
- Hosted baseline (warmed): p95 <= 120 ms, p99 <= 420 ms — PASS
- Cold-warm delta: documented but not a hard fail unless > 2x warmed p99
- Streaming: first-token <= 45 ms 95% and chunk tail <= 75 ms 95% during 300 concurrent sessions
- No more than 0.5% request error/timeout over the 2h window

Operational asks from customer (Samir):
- Provide the exact ingress timestamp field name used in traces (so we align event mapping)
- Confirm whether any traffic is routed through your tokenization/normalization proxy (would impact server-side token count)

I’ll start building the harness this week and will post the job spec to the shared drive. Jordan — once Samir confirms the 03/06 slot we’ll lock infra and run a dry run 24h prior.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
To: Samir Kaur <samir.kaur@noriahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed latency qualification plan

Samir — thanks for the trace bundle and for confirming 03/06. Two quick operational points and next steps: 

1) We ran a short dry run against a replay of ~10% of the trace bundle yesterday; preliminary results look promising — warmed p95 at ~98 ms and p99 at ~360 ms on the hosted config (this is internal and not yet the formal run). Will share formal artifacts after the 2h run.

2) Confirmed acceptance gates (per Ben’s draft) unless you want to tighten first-token to 35 ms. If you want that tighter gate we’ll need to run an additional streaming micro-optimization sweep (adds one day).

3) Calendar: we scheduled the official 2h hosted vs incumbent comparison for Tue 03/06 09:00–11:00 PDT and a 90min streaming stress run Wed 03/07 10:00–11:30 PDT. Invites sent; please accept.

4) Deliverables we’ll hand you within 48h of the final run: full NDJSON traces for both hosted and incumbent runs, p50/p90/p95/p99 histograms (edge-aligned), concurrency/session churn timeline, and a short exec one-pager highlighting risk areas and cost delta.

5) If you want us to also produce a quantized / lower-cost variant comparison we can include that as an optional appendix (helps with economics but may impact p99).

If all good I’ll mark the thread as ‘ready for run’ and Ben will kick off infra provisioning. 

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
